findings.title: HTML altChunk colspan can exhaust rendering memory
findings.summary: A small DOCX HTML altChunk can declare an arbitrarily large colspan. Rendering expands it into one generated XML grid column per value without an output budget, allowing document suppliers to exhaust CPU/memory.

severity.rationale: High process availability impact with medium deployment-dependent likelihood: the public renderer accepts caller-supplied documents, but a shared service deployment is not established. Caller OS resource limits reduce blast radius.
severity.changeConditions: Severity rises where an exposed shared renderer handles attacker-controlled documents without process isolation or quotas; strict worker CPU/memory limits reduce impact.

confidence.rationale: Static source establishes direct numeric parsing and unbounded proportional output before DOM construction; no runtime exploit was executed.

codeEvidence.label: Attacker-controlled span has no upper bound
codeEvidence.explanation: Any positive usize HTML span is retained; only invalid and zero values fall back to one.

codeEvidence.label: One output node is appended per declared column
codeEvidence.explanation: cols is the maximum sum of attacker-controlled spans in a row (469-475). A span of one billion requests one billion generated XML elements.

codeEvidence.label: Expansion occurs after source admission and before DOM parsing
codeEvidence.explanation: with_layout admits original bytes at 773-774, then resolves an internal chunk and builds expanded XML. Original compressed/inflated input limits do not bound generated output.

rootCause.summary: HTML colspan directly determines generated grid XML length without a column or output budget.

findings.remediation: Bound imported HTML colspan and aggregate column sums using checked arithmetic; enforce a generated XML/work budget and return a typed refusal before expansion.

counterEvidence: Original DOCX package is admitted before rendering (src/convert/mod.rs:773-774), but this limits input bytes rather than the numeric expansion.
Internal relationship resolution avoids network access; arbitrary network reads are not claimed.
SECURITY.md recommends process CPU/memory limits, which bound host impact but do not prevent the renderer from exhausting its worker budget.
limitations: No runtime reproduction, exploit input, or shared deployment verification was performed.
validation.summary: Parent independently traced altChunk parsing, end_table, and with_layout; no bound exists between numeric parsing and the append loop.

dataflow.summary: DOCX -> with_layout -> internal altChunk -> chunk_html/html_to_wml -> colspan parse -> end_table -> generated XML append per column -> exhaustion.

impact.rationale: Exhaustion or termination of the rendering process and its current work.

likelihood.rationale: Direct public parser boundary, but exposed multi-user service deployment is conditional.

reachability.summary: Public rendering APIs share with_layout, which expands internal HTML/MHT chunks after source admission and before DOM parsing.
reachability.attacker: Supplier of a document rendered by another caller
preconditions: Victim renders an attacker-supplied DOCX; either internal HTML/MHT altChunk or native OOXML table spans carry the numeric cardinality.

remediationTests: Use small deterministic HTML fixtures to verify a large numeric colspan is rejected before output construction; test exact column-budget boundaries, overflow of aggregate spans, and normal merged-cell behavior.
Test native gridSpan, gridBefore/gridAfter and combined-row occupancy at and beyond the budget, as well as aggregate arithmetic overflow.

codeEvidence.label: Native OOXML span is unrestricted
codeEvidence.explanation: Cell span becomes a usize with no cardinality cap.

codeEvidence.label: Span occupancy determines allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: A one-cell table with a billion-column span requests roughly 4 GB for f32 column widths alone; resolve_table_merges subsequently resizes its per-column open vector at 14637-14638.

rootCause.summary: Native table occupancy and merge vectors are sized from unrestricted gridSpan/grid-skip values without a table column budget.

candidate.title: Potential quadratic entity scanning in permissive XML DOM
candidate.originalEvidence: admission check_xml_depth ignores Event::GeneralRef (src/admission.rs:798-820), while permissive DOM unescape_xml_text scans to next ';' from every '&' and rebuilds body/decode char Vec per attempt (src/xmllinq/parse.rs:768-793). A compressed XML text run of repeated '&' ending in ';' may pass tolerant admission then trigger quadratic work.
candidate.counterEvidence: quick-xml refuses repeated bare '&' in ordinary text; original plain-text route is blocked. Admission deliberately tolerates unquoted attributes; revised comment-swallowing route must be validated independently.
candidate.additionalEvidence: One-character unquoted value whose character never reappears: permissive DOM (parse.rs:573-591) takes it as quote and scans to EOF, swallowing a comment with repeated bare '&'; admission sees the one-byte unquoted value and ignores comment content. WmlDocument::from_bytes -> main_document reaches quadratic unescape_xml_text. Strict inspect/checked XML APIs reject malformed attributes.

candidate.title: DTD parser differential bypasses XML depth limits
candidate.originalEvidence: quick-xml 0.42 DtdParser skips quoted ENTITY values including '>' and '<' (src/parser/dtd.rs:28-59,194-200,262-265); admission ignores DocType (src/admission.rs:819).
